integrity: The proof derives the envelope, feedback, projected scheduler map, null-step acceptance, and both dynamical regimes directly from the cited algorithm.
Finite exact-arithmetic checks are supplementary and are not used as a proof of the infinite statements.
The primary classification metadata inspected for arXiv:2609.10732 lists MSC 90C06 first, followed by 90C25 and 90C53.
limitations: The theorem is scalar and deterministic and uses the symmetric candidate interval [1,2/s-1].
No universality is claimed for other candidate sets, matrix preconditioners, varying online stepsizes, AdaGrad, or nonlinear splitting maps.
The scalar dynamics are affinely equivalent to projected hypergradient descent, leaving residual risk from older unindexed analyses of that exact recurrence.

title: A sharp online-learning phase transition for scalar OS-FBS
